question.problem:
Calculate the Cartesian equation of the circle

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0\le \theta <2\pi .
$$
question.worked_solution:
To find the Cartesian equation of the circle, we need to eliminate the parameter $\theta .$ We can do this using the Pythagorean theorem.

By squaring the $x$-equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ {x}^{2} & =(4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2} \\  & =16{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ,\end{aligned}
$$

By squaring the $y$-equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ {y}^{2} & =(4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2} \\  & =16{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations and using ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =16{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +16{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =16({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\  & =16(1) \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the Cartesian equation is ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=16.$
